mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volvo S60/V60 T8 engine replacement costs between £5,500 and £9,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, with fitting adding £1,000-£2,000 depending on your location and whether you choose a Volvo PHEV specialist or main dealer. Used B4204T34 or B4204T35 engines can be found from £2,500-£4,500, but come with no warranty and no upgraded components. One forum user reported an £11,000 engine replacement cost for their T8.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of ERAD failure in a Volvo S60/V60 T8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) is a common T8 failure point. Symptoms include hesitation on pulling away, pulling away then cutting out, juddering (axle tramp), or a loud clunking from the rear. If you experience any of these, get the codes read at a Volvo dealer immediately - if the car is within 4-5 years old, Volvo may contribute to the repair cost.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if your S60/V60 T8 is otherwise sound and has no major body or chassis issues. A 2018-2020 S60/V60 T8 values between £18,000 and £38,000, making a £5,500-£9,000 rebuilt engine replacement - around 15-30% of the car's value - a financially sound decision on higher-value examples. For older or higher-mileage examples under £15,000, evaluate carefully.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full Volvo S60/V60 T8 engine replacement typically takes 3-6 working days from delivery of the replacement engine. The complex PHEV powertrain requires additional time for hybrid system integration and calibration. Specialist fitters often complete the work in 3-4 days, while main dealers may take 5-6 days due to scheduling.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Volvo S60/V60 T8 engine codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T8 range includes several engine codes with different power outputs. B4204T28 (318hp, 2016-2018) is the earliest T8 unit. B4204T34 (303hp, 2018-2020) and B4204T35 (320hp, 2018-2024) are the most common UK variants. B4204T39 (333hp, 2019-2021) and B4204T48 (318hp, 2021-present) are Polestar Engineered variants. All are 2.0-litre turbo+supercharged petrol engines paired with a 65kW electric motor driving the rear axle.

mainEntity.name: Are Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEVs reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T8 powertrain is sophisticated and generally reliable when properly maintained, but the ERAD unit is a known weak point. The internal combustion engine itself is robust but the twin-charged (turbo + supercharger) setup adds complexity. Using the correct 0W-20 oil (Castrol Edge Professional V or VCC RBS0-2AE) and regular servicing are essential. The ERAD is covered by Volvo's extended warranty - 100% up to 4 years, 50% up to 5 years.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volvo S60 and V60 T8 Twin Engine plug-in hybrid represents the performance pinnacle of Volvo's mid-size range. Combining a 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbocharged and supercharged petrol engine with an electric motor driving the rear axle (ERAD - Electric Rear Axle Drive), the T8 delivers exceptional performance with low emissions. The T8 badge has evolved through multiple powertrain iterations since its debut, with increasing power outputs and improved electric range.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV - What It Costs to Fix, and When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV powertrains are among the most complex in the premium segment. The combination of a turbocharged and supercharged 2.0-litre petrol engine with an electric rear axle motor (ERAD) creates multiple failure points. The B4204T35 is the most common T8 engine in UK S60/V60 models, while the Polestar Engineered variants (B4204T39, B4204T48) demand even more specialist attention. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) Failure - "Why the Volvo S60/V60 T8 ERAD Fails Prematurely"
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine PHEV (all models, 2016-present)
problems.rootCause: The ERAD unit - a 65kW (87hp) electric motor driving the rear axle - is a known weak point on T8 models. Common symptoms include hesitation on pulling away, pulling away then cutting out, juddering (axle tramp), or a loud clunking from the rear. Volvo has extended warranty coverage for this part to 5 years: up to 4 years they pay 100%, up to 5 years they pay 50%.

repairOptions.longevity: If only gear wear; parts and labour circa £1.7k parts + 12 hours
If motor itself has failed; circa £9k cost
If internal combustion engine has failed; reported £11k cost

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2018-2022 Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin Engine sits in the £18,000-£38,000 value band. ERAD repair at £2,500-£3,500 is good value (8-15% of vehicle value). Full ERAD replacement at £6,000-£8,000 represents 15-30% of vehicle value - still viable on higher-value examples. Complete engine replacement at £7,500-£10,000 is 20-40% of vehicle value; evaluate carefully on older or higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: The ERAD is the most common T8-specific failure. If you experience any symptoms - especially hesitation or clunking - get the codes read at a Volvo dealer immediately. If the car is within 4-5 years old, Volvo may contribute to the cost. For the ICE engine itself, preventative maintenance (regular oil changes with Castrol Edge Professional V 0W-20) is essential. If the engine has failed, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components offers better reliability than a used engine of unknown provenance.

problems.h4: Supercharger and Cooling System Failure - "Why the Volvo S60/V60 T8 Twin-Charged Engine Loses Power"
problems.rootCause: The twin-charged (turbo + supercharger) setup adds complexity. The supercharger clutch can wear, causing a loss of low-end power. Cooling system components - water pump, thermostat housing, coolant pipes - use plastic fittings that degrade over time, leading to coolant leaks and potential overheating.

repairOptions.longevity: If clutch wear is detected early; prevents loss of low-end torque

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Water pump, thermostat, coolant pipes, expansion tank
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative at 70,000-80,000 miles; addresses common failure points
If overheating has caused head gasket or internal damage; only justified on high-value examples

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2023 Volvo S60/V60 T8 sits in the £20,000-£45,000 value band. Cooling system overhaul at £700-£1,200 is good preventative maintenance. Full engine replacement at £7,500-£10,000 represents 20-40% of vehicle value - a significant but often justifiable expense for a premium PHEV.
problems.recommendation: The T8's twin-charged engine is sophisticated but requires preventative maintenance. Replace the water pump and thermostat as a preventative measure at 70,000-80,000 miles. Use only the correct 0W-20 oil (Castrol Edge Professional V or VCC RBS0-2AE). If the supercharger clutch fails, replacing it early (£800-£1,400) is far cheaper than a full engine replacement.
